question: What will the first reported earnings per share after September 2026 be for the following companies? (Meta)

calls.reasoning: Consensus for Meta Q3 2026 EPS is ~6.4-6.8 (adjusted, excl. the ~$10B youth-settlement legal charge, ~$3.90/share). Meta typically beats underlying EPS (Q3'25 adj 7.25 vs ~6.7; Q2'26 ex-charges ~7.36 vs 7.22), so the adjusted-basis median is ~6.9. The key risk is the resolution basis: GAAP diluted EPS would be ~2.8-3.5, far below range; the question's range (centered ~6.35) and Nasdaq's listing of year-ago EPS as $7.25 (adjusted, not GAAP $1.05) suggest an adjusted data feed, so I put ~25% below the lower bound for GAAP resolution and ~14% above 7.345 for a strong beat. No human market found (Polymarket/Manifold none; Kalshi has Meta KPI/net-income markets but no matching EPS contract).
calls.dossier:
- Q2 2026 (reported Jul 29, 2026): GAAP diluted EPS $6.18 vs est $7.22; included $2.40B legal charges + $1.18B severance; revenue $60.8B (+28%); diluted shares 2,566M; tax rate 16% (stocktitan/Meta release).
- Q3 2026 guidance: revenue $61-64B; FY2026 total expenses $165-169B; tax rate 15-17% for remaining quarters (Meta Q2 release).
- Aug 26, 2026: Meta settled 29-state youth social-media case for up to $18B, paid over 10 years; expects ~$10B legal expense recognized in Q3 2026, not included in prior expense outlook (TechCrunch, cryptobriefing). Admiral Markets estimates ~$3.90/share impact.
- Consensus Q3 2026 EPS: TipRanks ~$6.77; Admiral ~$6.74-6.77 'adjusted, excluding legal charges'; Yahoo avg $6.25 (44 analysts); Nasdaq $6.39 (12 estimates) and lists year-ago EPS as $7.25 (Q3 2025 adjusted excl. ~$15.9B tax charge; GAAP Q3 2025 was $1.05).
- Revenue consensus ~$63.25B. Meta historically lands near/above top of revenue guidance.
- Recent beat history: Q3'25 adjusted 7.25 vs ~6.7 est; Q2'26 ex-charges ~7.36 vs 7.22 est.
- Report date: Admiral says Oct 28, 2026 after close; Nasdaq listed Nov 4.
- Resolution instrument: criteria blank; GAAP diluted EPS (~2.8-3.5 with charge) vs data-feed/adjusted EPS (~6.5-7.4) is the dominant ambiguity. Question range 5.345-7.345 centered near feed consensus.
- Event window: first EPS reported after Sept 2026 -> Q3 2026 report (~Oct 28); as of Oct 13 report not yet released.
- Searched, not found: Kalshi/Polymarket EPS contract for Meta Q3 (Kalshi has KPI/net income markets only); explicit statement on tax deductibility of the $10B charge.
calls.reference_class: Meta quarterly EPS actuals vs analyst consensus, 2024-2026 (beats typically 2-10%)

calls.reasoning: Meta reports Q3 2026 on Oct 21. It has said it will book about $10B of legal expense in Q3 for the youth-addiction settlement with the states. Meta reports only GAAP EPS, and in Q2 2026 data providers took the GAAP $6.18 (including $2.4B legal and $1.18B severance charges) as the reported EPS against a $7.17 consensus. Q3 operating income excluding the charge is roughly $22-23B at about $63-64B revenue; the charge costs about $3-3.9 per share, so GAAP EPS comes out near $3.5-4.3, below the 5.345 bound. Over 50% sits below the bound; 0.5 is the format cap. Excluding the charge, EPS is about $6.9-7.5 (consensus excluding the charge is about $6.77, plus Meta's usual beat), which can top 7.345. The resolution metric is unspecified, which is the main uncertainty. No human market was found: the harness found nothing on Polymarket or Manifold, and Kalshi and bookmakers were not separately checked.
calls.dossier:
- Meta will release Q3 2026 results after the market closes on Wed Oct 21, 2026 (Meta IR press release, Sept/Oct 2026).
- Q2 2026 actuals (reported about Aug 2026): revenue $60.80B (+28% y/y), GAAP diluted EPS $6.18 vs $7.14 a year earlier; costs and expenses $42.03B (+55%) including $2.40B legal charges and $1.18B severance; operating income $18.78B; tax rate 16%; net income $15.85B (TradingView 10-Q summary; Investing.com).
- Data providers (Investing.com) treated the GAAP $6.18 as the Q2 'actual' vs a $7.17 consensus, i.e. a $0.99 'miss'. Precedent: one-off charges were NOT stripped out of the headline reported EPS.
- Aug 26, 2026: Meta settled the multistate youth social-media addiction case with 29 state AGs for up to about $16.7-18B, paid in annual installments over 10 years (CNBC, Variety, Al Jazeera).
- Meta expects to recognize about $10B of legal expense in Q3 2026 for this settlement (Admiral Markets Oct 2026; CryptoBriefing). Sources conflict on whether the full-year expense guidance already included it.
- Tax deductibility of the charge was not found; fines paid to governments are generally non-deductible under US rules, restitution may be deductible. Guided tax rate is 15-17%.
- Q3 2026 revenue guidance: $61-64B; street revenue consensus about $63.2-63.3B. FY26 expense guidance $165-169B; capex $130-145B.
- Published Q3 EPS consensus figures conflict: about $6.74-6.77 (TipRanks/Admiral, apparently excluding the charge), $6.28 (KuCoin/MarketBeat-type), and $6.25 average of 44 analysts (Yahoo). Unclear how much of the charge each includes.
- Arithmetic: $10B pre-tax divided by about 2.57B diluted shares is about $3.9/share before tax, about $3.3 after a 16% tax benefit if deductible.
- Q3 2025 precedent: Meta booked a ~$15.9B one-time tax charge; GAAP EPS was $1.05 and Meta disclosed about $7.25 excluding the charge. Providers differed on which figure they reported (from memory, not re-verified this run).
- Resolution criteria text was blank. Not stated whether resolution uses GAAP diluted EPS or an adjusted/charge-excluded figure. This is the dominant uncertainty, since the two figures differ by about $3/share.
- Status quo: Meta reports GAAP EPS in its press release; one-off charges are typically shown in GAAP with a narrative 'excluding X' figure.
- Event window: Meta's first EPS report after Sept 2026, expected Oct 21, 2026, which is before the scheduled resolution of Oct 28, 2026; as of Oct 13 the report is 8 days away.
- Searched but not found: a human prediction market (harness checked Polymarket and Manifold; Kalshi and bookmakers not checked), an analyst GAAP-inclusive Q3 estimate, tax treatment of the settlement.
calls.reference_class: Meta quarterly diluted EPS vs consensus in quarters with large disclosed one-time charges (Q3 2025 tax charge, Q2 2026 legal and severance charges), where data providers' 'reported EPS' followed GAAP

calls.reasoning: Q3 2026 consensus EPS excluding the expected ~$10B youth-settlement legal charge is ~$6.3-6.8. Meta usually beats; Q2'26 ex-charges was ~$7.36, so adjusted Q3 centers ~$6.9 with real upside past 7.345. The question range (centered ~6.35 = consensus) and Nasdaq's use of adjusted $7.25 for Q3'25 suggest an adjusted feed resolves this. But GAAP EPS including the charge would be ~$3-4.3, and Investing.com used GAAP for Q2'26, so ~28% sits below the lower bound.
calls.reconciliation: The main dispute is whether the question resolves on GAAP or adjusted EPS. The blank criteria leave it unsettled. The range centered on consensus and the precedent of Nasdaq/Zacks using adjusted $7.25 for Q3'25 point toward adjusted. Investing.com using GAAP $6.18 for Q2'26 points toward GAAP. I weight GAAP at ~28%, between Run 2's 7% and Run 3's 50%, because evidence exists on both sides. Run 2 did not mention the ~$10B Q3 charge, but Runs 1 and 3 cite it from multiple independent sources, so I treat it as probably real. Report date (Oct 21 vs Oct 28 vs Nov 4) is unsettled but doesn't matter because Oct 21 and Oct 28 are both before resolution. Conditional on adjusted, all runs agree on a median ~6.8-6.9 with a beat skew; I carry that forward with an 18% upper escape given Q2's ex-charge 7.36.
